source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 5 May 1955, p. 6 ("Bangor (municipal nominations)"); North Down Herald and County Down Independent, 7 May 1955, p. 1 ("Dark-horse Magowan canters in - then out (Bangor nominations and withdrawals)")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: three nominations for three seats (Belfast News-Letter, 5 May 1955, p. 6, page image read); 'a fight in only one of Bangor's five wards' (Clifton) after withdrawals (North Down Herald, 7 May 1955, p. 1)

note: Municipal elections, 18 May 1955. Only Clifton Ward was contested. The four uncontested wards are from the nominations printed in the News-Letter of 5 May 1955; the North Down Herald (7 May 1955) reports that after Magowan's withdrawal in Ballyholme only Clifton was contested (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Four nominated; David J. H. Magowan withdrew, 'leaving Mayor David Ewart, Deputy Mayor Fred Tughan and Mr. Brice Smyth with no opposition' (North Down Herald, 7 May 1955, p. 1). The News-Letter prints 'Symth'. Returned unopposed.
